The agent began by diagnosing the baseline’s high latency. It wrote that large-k cases were “catastrophically compute-bound” and suspected dynamic indexing was spilling the top-k arrays into local memory. The proposed change was to template the insertion on K so that indices became compile-time constants.

The new CUDA implementation maintained a sorted, register-resident top-k list per thread, then merged thread lists through shared memory. Its insertion path was unrolled:

template <int K>
__device__ __forceinline__ void insert(float* tv, int* ti, float v, int idx) {
    if (v <= tv[K - 1]) return;
    float pv = v;  int pi = idx;
    #pragma unroll
    for (int p = 0; p < K; ++p) {
        bool take = (pv > tv[p]);
        float nv = take ? pv : tv[p];   int ni = take ? pi : ti[p];
        float dv = take ? tv[p] : pv;   int di = take ? ti[p] : pi;
        tv[p] = nv; ti[p] = ni; pv = dv; pi = di;
    }
}

The pairwise merge used separate source pointers, but advanced whichever pointer was selected without checking whether it had reached K:

int i = 0, j = 0;
for (int m = 0; m < K; ++m) {
    float a = Av[i], b = Bv[j];
    bool ta = (a >= b);
    // ...
    i += ta ? 1 : 0;
    j += ta ? 0 : 1;
}
